title: Derived categories and derived functors
statement:
All derived categories are unbounded. For an abelian category $\mathcal C$, $D(\mathcal C)$
is the localization of the category of cochain complexes in $\mathcal C$ at the
quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its bounded below part
$D^+(\mathcal C)\subseteq D(\mathcal C)$ is the full subcategory of complexes whose
cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. We work in the universes of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A K-injective complex $I$ means that every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic; K-flat means [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Grothendieck abelian means [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Derived functors are total
derived functors on the unbounded categories, computed on resolutions:

- **Right derived functors.** Let $\mathcal C$ have K-injective resolutions, i.e. every
  complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex. Then every additive
  functor $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ to an abelian category has a total right
  derived functor $RF\colon D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$, computed by applying $F$
  termwise to a K-injective resolution. Every Grothendieck abelian category has
  K-injective resolutions.
- **Left derived functors.** Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal abelian category with the
  following properties: its tensor product is additive in each variable; it has
  countable coproducts and exact $\mathbf Z$-indexed colimits, and tensoring with a
  fixed object on either side preserves both these coproducts and these colimits; and it has functorial flat resolutions: a functor $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ with a natural epimorphism $P(M)\to M$ and flat values, where flat means that tensoring on either side preserves short exact sequences. Let
  $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and send quasi-isomorphisms between
  K-flat complexes to quasi-isomorphisms. Then $F$ has a total left derived functor
  $LF\colon D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$, computed by applying $F$ termwise to a
  K-flat resolution. Pullback, tensor product and extension of scalars are derived
  this way.
- **Exact functors.** Under the respective existence hypotheses above, if $F$ is exact, then $RF\cong D(F)$ and $LF\cong D(F)$, where
  $D(F)$ applies $F$ termwise.
- **Derived adjunctions.** Let $f\colon\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D\colon g$ be
  an adjunction $f\dashv g$ of additive functors, with $f$ as in the second item and
  $\mathcal D$ with K-injective resolutions. Then $Lf\dashv Rg$.

Let $X$ be a scheme with the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The derived categories of this section are the following. In the last row, $\mathcal R$ is a ring object in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$, for $\mathcal A$ as in the first row. Constructibility means exactly [def-sfb-constructible-module]: there is a finite stratification of $X$ by locally closed subschemes such that on each stratum the restricted module is locally finitely presented over the restricted ring object [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. Local finite presentation allows arbitrary morphisms between finite free modules over that ring object; it does not require the presentation matrices to come from constant scalars. This is the predicate used in the master target. The reference to [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] is a forward reference, not input to the ambient derived category.

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ | $D(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A))$, finite coefficients (layer A). Here $\mathcal A$ is a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category and $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ carries the tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. |
| $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ | $D(\Mod(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab),\Lambda_X))$, non-finite coefficients (layer B), for the ring object $\Lambda_X$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and its module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E$ resp. $\underline E$ this is $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ resp. $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$. |
| $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$ | For a coefficient ring object $\mathcal R$ with the constructibility condition just fixed, the full subcategory of $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$ consisting of $K$ such that $H^i(K)=0$ outside a finite interval and every $H^i(K)$ is constructible in that sense. Morphisms are the ambient derived morphisms. |

proof.text: Use the localization and cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $D^+(\mathcal C)$ as the full subcategory on objects $K$ for which there is $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i<a$. This is a condition on the derived object: replacing a complex by a quasi-isomorphic one does not change its cohomology. No boundedness condition is imposed on $D(\mathcal C)$ itself.

For an additive $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, the source hypothesis of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] is exactly the assumed existence of K-injective resolutions. Its unit is invertible on K-injectives, so a resolution $K\to I$ computes $RF(K)$ as $F(I)$. If $\mathcal C$ is Grothendieck abelian, [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] supplies such a resolution for every unbounded complex; no bounded-below restriction is used.

Under the stated monoidal and resolution hypotheses, [lem-sfb-unbounded-kflat-resolution-existence] supplies a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat for every complex $K$. The functor-specific assumption is exactly [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Apply [def-sfb-left-derived-functor]: its counit is invertible on K-flat complexes, and therefore $LF(K)$ is represented by the termwise complex $F(P)$. This explains the resolution convention; it does not assert that an arbitrary additive functor preserves all quasi-isomorphisms.

In the respective source categories above, an exact $F$ has the canonical comparisons $RF\cong D(F)$ and $LF\cong D(F)$ by [def-sfb-right-derived-exact] and [def-sfb-left-derived-exact]. Both statements include the resolution hypotheses needed to define the indicated derived functor. Hence the exact-functor clause is read under those hypotheses.

For the adjunction clause, denote its unit by $\eta$ and counit by $\varepsilon$. For a chain map $a:f(P)\to I$, put $b^n=g(a^n)\eta_{P^n}$; then $g(d_I^n)b^n=g(d_I^na^n)\eta_{P^n}=g(a^{n+1})gf(d_P^n)\eta_{P^n}=b^{n+1}d_P^n$. Conversely, for a chain map $b:P\to g(I)$, put $a^n=\varepsilon_{I^n}f(b^n)$. Naturality gives $d_I^na^n=\varepsilon_{I^{n+1}}fg(d_I^n)f(b^n)=\varepsilon_{I^{n+1}}f(b^{n+1}d_P^n)=a^{n+1}f(d_P^n)$. The two triangle identities give $\varepsilon_{I^n}f(g(a^n)\eta_{P^n})=a^n$ and $g(\varepsilon_{I^n}f(b^n))\eta_{P^n}=b^n$. For a chain homotopy $a-a'=d_Ih+hd_{f(P)}$, additivity and naturality give $b^n-b'^n=g(d_I^{n-1})g(h^n)\eta_{P^n}+g(h^{n+1})\eta_{P^{n+1}}d_P^n$. Conversely a homotopy $b-b'=d_{g(I)}k+kd_P$ gives $a^n-a'^n=d_I^{n-1}\varepsilon_{I^{n-1}}f(k^n)+\varepsilon_{I^n}f(k^{n+1})f(d_P^n)$. Thus the mutually inverse operations descend to the homotopy categories of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Naturality of $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ also gives $(a f(v))^\sharp=a^\sharp v$ and $(wa)^\sharp=g(w)a^\sharp$ for chain maps $v$ and $w$. Therefore $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal D)}(f(P),I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal C)}(P,g(I))$ bifunctorially.

Fix a K-flat $P$ and a K-injective $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the left-hand side of the preceding bijection identifies with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal D)}(Qf(P),QI)$. We next show that the localization map $\theta:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal C)}(P,g(I))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal C)}(QP,Qg(I))$ is bijective. No claim that $g(I)$ is K-injective is made or needed.

For surjectivity of $\theta$, [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] gives the right calculus of fractions for $K(\mathcal C)$. By [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation], any map $QP\to Qg(I)$ has a roof $P\xleftarrow{s}Z\xrightarrow{a}g(I)$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Choose a K-flat resolution $r:T\to Z$ using [lem-sfb-unbounded-kflat-resolution-existence]. Put $t=sr$ and $a'=ar$. Both $T$ and $P$ are K-flat and $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $f(t)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Its precomposition map into $I$ is bijective by [lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle]. Consequently the transpose of $a'$ has the unique form $v\circ f(t)$ for $v:f(P)\to I$. If $b:P\to g(I)$ is the transpose of $v$, naturality of transposition gives $bt=a'$. Localizing yields $Q(b)=Q(a')Q(t)^{-1}=Q(a)Q(s)^{-1}$, as required.

For injectivity, suppose $b,c:P\to g(I)$ have equal images in $D(\mathcal C)$. Apply [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] to their roofs with identity denominators; it applies by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]. There is a quasi-isomorphism $u:Z\to P$ with $bu=cu$ in $K(\mathcal C)$. Resolve $Z$ by a K-flat $r:T\to Z$ using [lem-sfb-unbounded-kflat-resolution-existence]. Then $ur:T\to P$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes. By [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] its image under $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Transpose $bur=cur$ and use injectivity of precomposition with $f(ur)$ into $I$, given by [lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle]. The transposes of $b$ and $c$ are equal, hence $b=c$. This proves bijectivity of $\theta$.

For arbitrary derived objects $K,L$, choose $P\to K$ K-flat and $L\to I$ K-injective. Existence on the source is [lem-sfb-unbounded-kflat-resolution-existence], and existence on the target is the hypothesis of the adjunction clause. The comparisons in [def-sfb-left-derived-functor] and [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], together with the bijections just proved, give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal D)}(Lf(K),L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal D)}(f(P),I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal C)}(P,g(I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal C)}(K,Rg(L)).$$
The first comparison uses [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. To verify naturality on all derived morphisms, represent a map between K-flat representatives by a roof using [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] and [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation], and replace its middle object by a K-flat resolution. Transposition commutes with each resulting map of complexes, and therefore with the inverse of a quasi-isomorphism between them. Naturality of the left-derived counit identifies these inverse images with the maps of $Lf$. A map between K-injective target representatives is represented by a homotopy class by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; transposition commutes with that map, and naturality of the right-derived unit identifies its image with the map of $Rg$. Thus every square of the displayed Hom bijection commutes. A bifunctorial Hom bijection is precisely an adjunction, proving $Lf\dashv Rg$.

For the table, the small representative of the pro-étale site is supplied by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Each tensor functor of $\mathcal A$ is a left adjoint by closedness and symmetry, so it preserves zero and finite coproducts. In an abelian category these are finite biproducts; their projections are determined by the injections and zero maps, so preservation also preserves the diagonal and codiagonal formulas for addition. Thus tensor is additive in each variable, as required to apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] to this essentially small site and the given closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck category $\mathcal A$. This supplies an abelian sheaf category and hence its localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For layer B, [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] supplies the actual ring object $\Lambda_X$, and [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] supplies its module category. Closedness of the sheaf tensor [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] makes $\Lambda_X\otimes-$ preserve finite colimits, so [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] makes the module category abelian, even when $\Lambda$ is noncommutative. For the last row, $\mathcal R$ is a ring object in the same closed monoidal abelian sheaf category. Its tensor functor $\mathcal R\otimes-$ is a left adjoint and preserves finite colimits; [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] therefore makes $\Mod_{\mathcal R}$ abelian. Localizing each of these abelian module categories at quasi-isomorphisms gives its unbounded derived category. The symbols with $\mathcal O_E$ and $E$ abbreviate the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings; no constant or completed coefficient sheaf is substituted.

proof.text: The unit's fifth proof paragraph requires more than typing the table. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ is Grothendieck abelian, and its tensor preserves all colimits. Thus right derived functors exist by step 2. If $\mathcal A$ has a functorial flat resolution, [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution] transfers it to this sheaf category. Small colimits and exact filtered colimits are part of [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]; in particular the required countable coproducts and exact ordered-$\mathbf Z$ colimits exist. The tensor-colimit conclusion of the sheaf theorem gives their preservation on both sides. All hypotheses of step 3 are therefore met: every additive functor from this sheaf category that preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes has the stated total left derived functor. The hypothesis that $\mathcal A$ has a functorial flat resolution is retained.

proof.text: For layer B with commutative $\Lambda$, first construct the base flat resolution in $\Ab$. Put $P(M)=\bigoplus_{m\in |M|}\mathbf Z$ and send the generator $[m]$ to $m$. A homomorphism $u:M\to N$ sends $[m]$ to $[u(m)]$, so $P$ is a functor and the augmentation is natural. It is surjective, since $m$ is the image of $[m]$; a surjective group map is epic since two homomorphisms equal on all its images are equal. The standard closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck structure on $\Ab$ is the example specified in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The unit $\mathbf Z$ is flat because its tensor functors are isomorphic to the identity by the unitors. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct] every $P(M)$ preserves finite limits under tensoring (symmetry gives both tensor sides). Closedness makes these tensor functors left adjoints, hence they also preserve finite colimits; therefore they are exact and $P(M)$ is flat in the short-exact-sequence sense used here. Applying [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$ gives functorial flat resolutions in $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] applied to $\mathcal A=\Ab$ and the essentially small site of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $\mathcal C$ is a Grothendieck abelian category whose sheafified tensor product is symmetric monoidal, closed and additive in each variable; these are the hypotheses on $\mathcal C$ of the module statements used next. The pulled-back ring $\Lambda_X$ is commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], so [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] now applies to $\mathcal C$ and $\Lambda_X$. Moreover [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] gives Grothendieck abelianness, [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] gives the symmetric relative tensor, and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] gives its right adjoints. A tensor functor therefore preserves colimits: $\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes_{\Lambda_X}\operatorname{colim}_iN_i,T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{colim}_iN_i,\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_X}(M,T))\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(N_i,\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_X}(M,T))\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes_{\Lambda_X}N_i,T)$. Symmetry identifies the other tensor functor $N\mapsto N\otimes_{\Lambda_X}M$ naturally with $N\mapsto M\otimes_{\Lambda_X}N$; therefore it preserves the same colimits. Each relative tensor functor preserves zero and finite coproducts. These are biproducts in the abelian module category, with projections determined by injections and zero morphisms, so the diagonal-codiagonal formula for addition is preserved. Hence the relative tensor is additive in both variables. The Grothendieck colimits and the flat resolutions just constructed meet all hypotheses of steps 2 and 3, proving right-derived existence for every additive functor and left-derived existence for every additive functor preserving K-flat quasi-isomorphisms in this commutative layer-B case. The source's symmetric-monoidal assertion cannot be applied to general noncommutative rings: the usual relative tensor of two left modules is not defined without converting one to a right module. For example a general pair of left $M_2(\mathbf Z)$-modules has no specified such conversion. For an arbitrary ring object the table asserts only the ambient abelian derived category, not this symmetric-monoidal flat-resolution conclusion.

proof.text: Use the constructibility predicate of [def-sfb-constructible-module], with its stated finite stratification and transported restriction to each stratum. The local condition is precisely [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. Its finite presentations are the arbitrary module morphisms and cokernels of [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], not presentations restricted to scalar constant matrices. This is exactly the master source's $\operatorname{IsConstructible}$ and $\operatorname{IsLocallyFinitelyPresented}$ definitions. No comparison with finite constant local models is required. The cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] assign $H^i(K)$ to every derived object. Require $H^i(K)=0$ outside a finite interval and require each $H^i(K)$ to satisfy that predicate. The full subcategory on these objects retains all ambient derived morphisms. This gives the last table row without using the later bounded-constructible node as an input, and without altering the master target's constructibility predicate.

lean.statement:
def rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions :
    DerivedCategory C ⥤ DerivedCategory D
lean.note: §1(B), existing convention interfaces: no lean record existed. This unit fixes several conventions rather than a new category: DerivedCategory/Q and DerivedCategory.Plus are Mathlib localization/full-subcategory definitions; IsKInjective is Mathlib's homotopy-vanishing condition.
